Search this repository very thoroughly for the server-push live events mechanism used to push events to browsers. I need to find:

1. The mechanism used (WebSocket, SSE/Server-Sent Events, long polling, etc.)
2. The "hub" implementation file where connections are managed
3. Which "memo" handlers broadcast events through the hub

Search for terms like: SSE, Server-Sent Events, WebSocket, EventSource, hub, broadcast, memo, live, push, event stream, text/event-stream. Look in server-side code. Check for any hub struct or class that manages client connections and broadcasts. Also search for "memo" handlers that call broadcast or similar methods on the hub.

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

19	// newIntegrationService builds a minimal APIV1Service backed by an in-memory
20	// SQLite database.  The store is closed automatically via t.Cleanup.
21	func newIntegrationService(t *testing.T) *APIV1Service {
22		t.Helper()
23		ctx := context.Background()
24		st := teststore.NewTestingStore(ctx, t)
25		t.Cleanup(func() { st.Close() })
26		p := &profile.Profile{Demo: true, Data: t.TempDir(), Driver: "sqlite", DSN: ":memory:"}
27		return NewAPIV1Service("test-secret", p, st)
28	}

30	// userCtx returns a context that authenticates as the given user.
31	func userCtx(ctx context.Context, userID int32) context.Context {
32		return context.WithValue(ctx, auth.UserIDContextKey, userID)
33	}
34	
35	// collectEventsFor reads events from ch for the given duration and returns them.
36	func collectEventsFor(ch <-chan []byte, d time.Duration) []string {
37		var out []string
38		deadline := time.After(d)
39		for {
40			select {
41			case data := <-ch:
42				out = append(out, string(data))
43			case <-deadline:
44				return out
45			}
46		}
47	}

49	// ---- context suppression ----
50	
51	func TestSuppressSSEContext(t *testing.T) {
52		ctx := context.Background()
53	
54		t.Run("default context is not suppressed", func(t *testing.T) {
55			assert.False(t, isSSESuppressed(ctx))
56		})
57	
58		t.Run("withSuppressSSE marks context as suppressed", func(t *testing.T) {
59			assert.True(t, isSSESuppressed(withSuppressSSE(ctx)))
60		})
61	
62		t.Run("suppression does not bleed into parent context", func(t *testing.T) {
63			suppressed := withSuppressSSE(ctx)
64			_ = suppressed
65			assert.False(t, isSSESuppressed(ctx))
66		})
67	}
68	
69	// ---- CreateMemoComment double-broadcast fix ----
70	
71	func TestCreateMemoComment_NoDuplicateSSEBroadcast(t *testing.T) {
72		ctx := context.Background()
73		svc := newIntegrationService(t)
74	
75		// Create an admin so the store is initialised, then a regular commenter.
76		author, err := svc.Store.CreateUser(ctx, &store.User{
77			Username: "author", Role: store.RoleAdmin, Email: "author@example.com",
78		})
79		require.NoError(t, err)
80		commenter, err := svc.Store.CreateUser(ctx, &store.User{
81			Username: "commenter", Role: store.RoleUser, Email: "commenter@example.com",
82		})
83		require.NoError(t, err)
84	
85		authorCtx := userCtx(ctx, author.ID)
86		commenterCtx := userCtx(ctx, commenter.ID)
87	
88		// Create a public memo so the commenter can react.
89		parent, err := svc.CreateMemo(authorCtx, &v1pb.CreateMemoRequest{
90			Memo: &v1pb.Memo{Content: "parent memo", Visibility: v1pb.Visibility_PUBLIC},
91		})
92		require.NoError(t, err)
93	
94		// Subscribe after the parent memo is created so the memo.created event
95		// for the parent does not pollute the assertion window.
96		client := svc.SSEHub.Subscribe(author.ID, store.RoleAdmin)
97		defer svc.SSEHub.Unsubscribe(client)
98	
99		// Create a comment.  Before the fix, this fired both memo.created (for the
100		// comment memo) and memo.comment.created (for the parent).
101		_, err = svc.CreateMemoComment(commenterCtx, &v1pb.CreateMemoCommentRequest{
102			Name:    parent.Name,
103			Comment: &v1pb.Memo{Content: "a comment", Visibility: v1pb.Visibility_PUBLIC},
104		})
105		require.NoError(t, err)
106	
107		// Give the synchronous broadcast a moment to land in the buffer, then
108		// collect everything that arrived.
109		events := collectEventsFor(client.events, 150*time.Millisecond)
110	
111		require.Len(t, events, 1, "expected exactly one SSE event for a comment creation, got: %v", events)
112		assert.True(t, strings.Contains(events[0], `"memo.comment.created"`),
113			"expected memo.comment.created, got: %s", events[0])
114	}

---

## Server-Push Live Events Mechanism

### 1. Mechanism: SSE (Server-Sent Events)

The project uses **Server-Sent Events (SSE)** -- not WebSocket or long polling. The SSE endpoint is registered at `GET /api/v1/sse` and streams `text/event-stream` content to authenticated browser clients.

- **Server endpoint**: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go` -- the `handleSSE` function sets headers `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, `Connection: keep-alive`, and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (to disable nginx buffering). It writes `data: <JSON>\n\n` frames and sends `: heartbeat\n\n` comment frames every 30 seconds to keep the connection alive.

- **Client consumer**: `/bench/home/work/web/src/hooks/useLiveMemoRefresh.ts` -- a React hook (`useLiveMemoRefresh`) that uses the native `fetch` API with a streaming `ReadableStream` reader (not `EventSource`) to connect to `/api/v1/sse` with a `Bearer` token. It parses `data:` lines, handles reconnection with exponential backoff (1s initial, 30s max, x2 multiplier), and invalidates React Query caches when events arrive.

### 2. Hub Implementation: `SSEHub`

**File**: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`

The `SSEHub` struct manages all active SSE client connections. Key design:

- **`SSEHub` struct** (line 56): holds a `sync.RWMutex`, a `map[*SSEClient]struct{}` of connected clients, and a `closed` bool.
- **`SSEClient` struct** (line 48): holds a buffered `chan []byte` (capacity 32), plus `userID` and `role` for visibility-based filtering.
- **`Subscribe(userID, role)`** (line 71): creates a new `SSEClient`, adds it to the map, returns it.
- **`Unsubscribe(client)`** (line 89): removes client from the map and closes its channel.
- **`Broadcast(event)`** (line 115): serializes the event to JSON, iterates all clients, checks `canReceive()` for visibility-based filtering (private memos are only sent to the creator and admins), and does a non-blocking send to each client's channel (dropping events for slow clients rather than blocking).
- **`Close()`** (line 99): disconnects all clients (used during server shutdown).

The hub is instantiated in `NewAPIV1Service` at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go` (line 57) and stored as `APIV1Service.SSEHub` (line 36). It is wired to the Echo router at line 125 via `RegisterSSERoutes`.

### 3. Memo Handlers That Broadcast Events

Six SSE event types are defined (in `sse_hub.go` lines 14-21):
- `memo.created`
- `memo.updated`
- `memo.deleted`
- `memo.comment.created`
- `reaction.upserted`
- `reaction.deleted`

The following service methods call `s.SSEHub.Broadcast(...)`:

| Handler Method | File | Line | Event Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CreateMemo` | `memo_service.go` | 163 | `memo.created` (suppressed when called from `CreateMemoComment` via `withSuppressSSE` context) |
| `UpdateMemo` | `memo_service.go` via `memo_update_helpers.go` | 513 -> 71 | `memo.updated` (via `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`) |
| `DeleteMemo` | `memo_service.go` | 585 | `memo.deleted` |
| `CreateMemoComment` | `memo_service_comments.go` | 126 | `memo.comment.created` (after suppressing the inner `CreateMemo`'s `memo.created` event) |
| `SetMemoAttachments` | `memo_attachment_service.go` | 48 | `memo.updated` (via `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`) |
| `SetMemoRelations` | `memo_relation_service.go` | 48 | `memo.updated` (via `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`) |
| `UpsertMemoReaction` | `reaction_service.go` | 106 | `reaction.upserted` (via `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent` helper) |
| `DeleteMemoReaction` | `reaction_service.go` | 161 | `reaction.deleted` (via `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent` helper) |

### Supporting Files

- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_event_helpers.go` -- contains `resolveSSECreatorID` (determines the creator ID for visibility filtering, using the parent memo's creator for comments) and `buildMemoReactionSSEEvent` (constructs SSE events for reaction operations with proper parent/visibility fields).
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub_test.go` -- unit tests for the hub (subscribe/unsubscribe, broadcast to multiple clients, private event scoping, slow client drop behavior).
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_service_test.go` -- integration tests verifying correct SSE behavior (no duplicate broadcasts for comments, reaction events carry correct visibility, attachment/relation updates emit `memo.updated`).
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/test/sse_handler_test.go` -- HTTP-level test for the SSE handler endpoint.

### Double-Broadcast Prevention

The `CreateMemoComment` handler (in `memo_service_comments.go` line 56) calls `CreateMemo` internally but wraps the context with `withSuppressSSE(ctx)` to prevent the inner `CreateMemo` from also broadcasting a `memo.created` event. Instead, only a single `memo.comment.created` event is emitted for the parent memo. This is defined in `memo_service.go` lines 22-36 using a context key (`suppressSSEKey`).
